src.q: Each film-coated tablet contains 10 mg dydrogesterone.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Progesterone insufficiency: dysmenorrhoea, endometriosis, irregular cycles, premenstrual syndrome. HRT: added to oestrogen in women with a uterus. Dysfunctional bleeding or secondary amenorrhoea (with an oestrogen).

src.q: Treatment of dysmenorrhoea, endometriosis, irregular menstrual cycles and pre-menstrual syndrome.
Dydrogesterone is used to supplement an estrogen treatment in non-hysterectomised women
Dysfunctional bleeding or secondary amenorrhoea: The drug may be used with an estrogen in the management of these conditions.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK SmPC accessed (emc 10 mg film-coated tablets).

items.t: Dysmenorrhoea: 10 mg twice daily, days 5-25. Endometriosis: 10 mg two to three times daily, days 5-25 or continuously. Irregular cycles: 10 mg twice daily, days 11-25. Premenstrual syndrome: 10 mg twice daily, days 12-26 (may be increased).

src.q: Dysmenorrhoea: 10 mg of dydrogesterone twice a day from day 5 to 25 of the cycle. Endometriosis: 10 mg of dydrogesterone two to three times daily from day 5 to 25 of the cycle, or continuously.
Irregular menstrual cycles : 10 mg of dydrogesterone twice a day from day 11 to 25 of the cycle. Pre-menstrual syndrome: 10 mg of dydrogesterone twice a day from day 12 to 26 of the cycle.

items.t: HRT with oestrogen: 10 mg daily for the last 14 days of each 28-day cycle (continuous sequential) or the last 12-14 days of oestrogen use (cyclical); may increase to 20 mg daily.

src.q: sequential supplementation of 10 mg dydrogesterone during the last 14 days of each 28-day cycle
Depending on the clinical response, the dosage may be adjusted to 20 mg dydrogesterone daily in the course of the treatment.

items.t: Dysfunctional uterine bleeding: to stop a bleed 10 mg twice daily for 5-7 days; continuing treatment 10 mg twice daily, days 11-25. Secondary amenorrhoea: 10 mg twice daily, days 11-25 (endometrium primed with oestrogen).

src.q: When treatment is started to arrest a bleeding episode 10 mg of dydrogesterone twice a day for five to seven days. For continuous treatment 10 mg of dydrogesterone twice a day from day 11 to day 25 of the cycle.
Secondary amenorrhoea: 10 mg of dydrogesterone twice a day from day 11 to 25

items.t: No relevant use before menarche. Safety and efficacy in adolescents 12-18 years not established; no dose recommendation.

src.q: There is no relevant use for dydrogesterone before menarche. The safety and efficacy of dydrogesterone in adolescents aged 12-18 years has not been established.

items.t: Hypersensitivity; known or suspected progestogen-dependent tumours; meningioma or history of meningioma; unexplained vaginal bleeding; contraindications to oestrogen when used together.

src.q: Known or suspected progestogen-dependent tumours - Meningioma or history of meningioma - Unexplained vaginal bleeding - Contraindications for the use of estrogens should be considered when used in combination with dydrogesterone

items.t: Severe acute and chronic liver disease; disorders of bilirubin metabolism (e.g. Dubin-Johnson, Rotor syndrome); previous or existing liver tumours; thrombophlebitis and thromboembolic diseases.

src.q: Severe acute and chronic liver diseases as well as disorders in the metabolism of bile pigments (e.g. Dubin-Johnson syndrome, Rotor syndrome) - Previous or existing liver tumours - Thrombophlebitis and thromboembolic diseases.

items.t: Find the cause of irregular bleeding before treating; investigate bleeding that occurs later in treatment or after it (endometrial biopsy may be needed).

src.q: If dydrogesterone is prescribed for the treatment of irregular bleeding, the etiology of this bleeding should be clarified.

items.t: Monitor closely, and consider stopping, if porphyria, depression, abnormal liver function from liver disease, or cholestatic jaundice/pruritus is present now or in the past (or worsened in pregnancy or previous hormone treatment).

src.q: discontinuation of treatment should be considered: - Porphyria - Depression - Pathological liver function values caused by acute or chronic liver disease - Cholestatic jaundice and/or pruritus

items.t: Meningioma has been reported: monitor for signs; stop if meningioma is diagnosed.

src.q: If a patient is diagnosed with meningioma, any dydrogesterone-containing treatment must be stopped

items.t: Persistent clinically significant hypertension: stop and treat. At higher doses caution with current or past cerebral apoplexy (stroke).

src.q: if persistent clinically significant hypertension develops during the use of dydrogesterone, it is advisable to discontinue dydrogesterone and to treat the hypertension
In higher doses, caution is advised with: - Cerebral apoplexy (also in the medical history)

items.t: With oestrogen as HRT: breast cancer, ovarian cancer, VTE (contraindicated in known thrombophilia), coronary disease and ischaemic stroke risks apply; review at least yearly.

src.q: Patients with known thrombophilia have an increased risk of VTE. HRT may add to this risk and is therefore contraindicated in these patients.
a careful appraisal of the risks and benefits should be undertaken at least annually

items.t: Contains lactose: people with galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: CYP enzyme inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, rifampicin, St John's wort) may increase dydrogesterone metabolism and reduce its effect.

src.q: the metabolism of dydrogesterone and DHD may be increased when used concomitantly with substances known to induce CYP enzyme activity
Clinically, increased dydrogesterone metabolism may lead to reduced effect.

items.t: Dydrogesterone does not inhibit or induce CYP enzymes at clinical concentrations (in vitro).

src.q: In vitro studies have shown that dydrogesterone and DHD at clinically relevant concentrations do not have an inhibitory or inducing effect on drug-metabolizing CYP enzyme

renal.note: No renal impairment advice in the UK SmPC accessed (emc 10 mg film-coated tablets).

items.t: Contraindicated in severe acute and chronic liver disease and liver tumours. Pathological liver function values from liver disease: monitor closely and consider stopping.

src.q: Severe acute and chronic liver diseases
Pathological liver function values caused by acute or chronic liver disease

items.t: Not authorised for use in pregnancy. No evidence of harm so far despite wide exposure; some progestogens have been linked to hypospadias but no firm conclusion can be drawn.

src.q: Nalvee 10 mg is not authorised for use in pregnancy.
So far there is no evidence of any harmful effect of dydrogesterone use during pregnancy.
The literature suggests that some progestogens are associated with an increased risk of hypospadias.

items.t: No data; progestogens pass into milk in small amounts and risk to the baby is unknown. Should not be taken while breastfeeding.

src.q: It is not known whether there is any risk to the baby. Therefore, Nalvee 10 mg should not be taken while breastfeeding.

items.t: No evidence that dydrogesterone reduces fertility at therapeutic doses.

src.q: There is no evidence that dydrogesterone decreases fertility at therapeutic doses.

items.t: Common: headache, migraine, nausea, menstrual disorders, breast pain or tenderness.

src.q: The most commonly reported adverse reactions in patients treated with dydrogesterone in clinical trials on indications without estrogen use are migraine/headache, nausea, menstrual disorders and breast pain/tension.

items.t: Mild somnolence or dizziness may occur, mainly in the first hours after a dose; take care driving or using machines.

src.q: Dydrogesterone may rarely cause mild somnolence and/or dizziness, especially during the first hours after use. Therefore, machines and vehicles should only be operated with caution.

items.t: Meningioma (growth of progestogen-dependent tumours): stop if diagnosed.

src.q: Increase in size of progestogen dependent tumours (e.g. meningioma)
If a patient is diagnosed with meningioma, any dydrogesterone-containing treatment must be stopped

items.t: Rare: abnormal liver function with jaundice, haemolytic anaemia, angioedema. Stop at once with migraine-like or unusually severe headache or sudden visual impairment.

src.q: Hepatic function abnormal (with asthenia or malaise, jaundice and abdominal pain)
migraine-like or unusually severe headache - acute vision impairment

items.t: Clarify the cause of irregular bleeding before starting; for HRT take a full personal and family history and examine as indicated.

src.q: If dydrogesterone is prescribed for the treatment of irregular bleeding, the etiology of this bleeding should be clarified.
Before starting or resuming HRT, a complete personal and family medical history should be obtained.

items.t: Monitor for meningioma signs; watch blood pressure; monitor closely with porphyria, depression, liver disease or cholestasis.

src.q: Patients should be monitored for signs and symptoms of meningiomas in accordance with clinical practice.

items.t: Stop: meningioma; persistent significant hypertension; migraine-like or unusually severe headache; acute visual impairment; VTE during HRT.

src.q: Therapy is to be discontinued immediately if there is a contraindication and if one of the following situations occurs: - migraine-like or unusually severe headache - acute vision impairment
If VTE develops after initiation of HRT, the drug must be discontinued.

items.t: Oral. Take at the same time each day; if twice daily, one in the morning and one in the evening.

src.q: When taking 2 film-coated tablets daily, it is recommended to take one in the morning and one in the evening.

items.t: Report painful leg swelling, sudden chest pain or breathlessness, severe headache or sudden vision problems at once. May cause mild drowsiness or dizziness.

src.q: especially painful swelling of a leg, sudden chest pain, dyspnoea
Dydrogesterone may rarely cause mild somnolence and/or dizziness
